html:
Babur was a Central Asian prince who founded the Mughal Empire in India. He was born in 1483 in the Fergana valley, a great great great grandson of Timur on his father's side and descended from Genghis Khan through his mother.

He spent his youth fighting for Timur's old capital, Samarkand. He took it three times and lost it each time, at last to the Uzbeks of the Shaybanid line. In 1504 he seized Kabul and made it his base for twenty years.

From Kabul he raided the Punjab, then struck at the Delhi Sultanate. In 1526 he beat Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat, using field guns and matchlocks. In 1527 he beat the Rajput leader Rana Sanga at Khanwa. He died in Agra in 1530 and was later buried in a garden in Kabul.

He left one of the great memoirs of any ruler, the Baburnama, written in Chagatai Turkish. It is frank about his defeats and drinking, and full of notes on plants, birds and gardens. His son Humayun nearly lost the new empire.
